findings.detail: REAL, AND I BROKE IT MYSELF RATHER THAN TAKING THE REPORT'S WORD. unfinished.detail:
The cache key is (data identity, start, len(data)) plus the stamp plus, since this round, the drawn flag. `labels` IS AN ARGUMENT OF tokenize AND IS IN NEITHER. The cached Segmentation carries `labels=out_labels` computed from the labels of the call that built it, so a later call with the same bytes object and a DIFFERENT `labels` argument -- including the None -> not-None direction -- is handed the earlier call's label vector and counted as tok.retok_noop, the same row whose meaning is 'the rebuild would have been byte-identical'. It is byte-identical in `ids` and `byte_pos` and NOT in `labels`, and the fix this round made stops at the dropout dimension.
MEASURED on the committed tree at the shipped TOK_DROPOUT=0.0 (my script, outside the repo), one Vocabulary, three calls on the SAME bytes object:
  s0 = tokenize(tk, v, data)                 -> s0.labels is None
  s1 = tokenize(tk, v, data, labels=[0]*n)   -> s1.labels is None      and `s1 is s0` -> True
  s2 = tokenize(tk, v, data, labels=[7]*n)   -> s2.labels is None      and `s2 is s0` -> True
  counters: {..., tok.segment: 1, tok.byte_fallback: 45, tok.retok_noop: 2}
A caller that asked for per-token labels got None, twice, with the ledger reporting two no-op re-segmentations. tokenize's own docstring makes labels load-bearing ('A token spans bytes and therefore could span a splice seam; it takes the label of its FIRST byte ... so a per-area score and a byte offset always agree') and the one live call site, spine/compose.py's `tok_api.tokenize(tok, sysm.vocab, sysm.stream.bytes, sysm.stream.labels, regularize=True, seed=int(run.seed))`, does pass them -- so the per-area label channel DOM and EVAL read is what a wrong hit silently substitutes. Not reachable in today's single-call-site pipeline, same as the dropout arm was not; reachable the moment the held-out/final segmentation callers P4 owes are written.
THE FIX, in the same shape the drawn-flag fix took -- the entry stays a valid STAMP and becomes an invalid ANSWER for a call that asked for different labels. Two exact edits, each appearing once in src/tok/api.py:

FIND (exact):
    if is_retok and drop <= 0.0 and cache[3] == stamp and not cache[5]:
REPLACE WITH:
    if is_retok and drop <= 0.0 and cache[3] == stamp and not cache[5] and cache[6] is labels:

FIND (exact):
    vocab._retok_cache = (data, start, len(data), stamp, seg, drop > 0.0)
REPLACE WITH:
    vocab._retok_cache = (data, start, len(data), stamp, seg, drop > 0.0, labels)

...with the seventh field named in Vocabulary.__init__'s tuple comment beside the sixth (FIND '# (data, start, len(data), stamp, Segmentation, drawn_with_dropout); None until the first' / REPLACE '# (data, start, len(data), stamp, Segmentation, drawn_with_dropout, labels); None until the first'). Identity rather than equality is deliberate and matches `cache[0] is data`: it is O(1), and the composition root hands the same list object back on a re-tokenization of its own stream, so the skip still fires on the path it was measured for (2.189 b/B, 68 points of word quality). VERIFY WITH: the three-call script above must print 's1.labels == [0]*n' and 's2.labels == [7]*n', while the two-identical-calls neighbour (same data, same labels object, twice) must still print 'same object? True' and tok.retok_noop 1. NO CHECK IN THE SUITE FAILS TODAY.

LOW SEVERITY AND I WILL NOT INFLATE IT: it cannot fire today, because nothing in the tree retires anything yet -- there is no `retire()` method on Vocabulary and tok/api.py::judge_probation and ::mint_burst are both `raise NotImplementedError`. Recording it because the round's fix was about exactly this cache and because the invariant's own justification is one implementation detail deep. src/tok/api.py::_segment consults TWO structures: `s2i.get(...)` and `if j is None or j in retired: continue`. The stamp is `(vocab.size(), len(vocab.seq2id))` and covers only the first. It works today solely because judge_probation's docstring promises retirement 'pops the bytes from the match table' -- i.e. it happens to move seq2id too. Two shapes defeat it once those bodies exist: (i) a retire that adds to `vocab.retired` without popping seq2id moves neither term of the stamp; (ii) a retire of one id and a REINSTATEMENT of a different already-retired id in the same flush (mint_burst's docstring makes reinstatement a real operation: 'put the old id back in the match table, mint nothing') moves len(seq2id) by -1 then +1 for a net zero while the match table has genuinely changed. Either way tokenize would take the skip and return a Segmentation containing a token the vocabulary no longer matches, counted as tok.retok_noop. THE FIX IS ONE TERM, and it costs nothing:

FIND (exact, appears once in src/tok/api.py):
